correctness.rationale: For every f>=1, in a binary normal basis, the coordinatewise square rotates the f binary coefficient vectors, and the fixed equation x=A x^[2] forces v_j=A^j v_0 and (A^f-I)v_0=0. This proves the exact idempotent count without a heuristic. Fitting's decomposition removes nilpotent primary components and proves least period M by the full fixed-space maximum. Primary-block gcd computations give the complete elementary-divisor formula. Direct independent exhaustive checks of every binary matrix in dimensions <=3 over F2, F4, F8, plus selected 4x4 over F16, and cycle tests, returned VERIFY_OK; these are corroborations rather than infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The graph evolution algebra and finite characteristic-two framework is from Elduque--Labra (arXiv:1902.02191v1) and Reis--Cadavid (arXiv:2006.11934v1), whose inspected results concern automorphisms and derivations; they do not imply counts of idempotent *elements* over every extension. Wei--Zou (arXiv:2310.12368v1) counts isomorphism classes of *perfect algebras*, not elementwise solutions x^2=x, on the accessible abstract; its full text was unavailable. Garcia-Martinez--Perez-Rodriguez (2026, DOI below) states the general idempotent equation but works on complex-field existence/completeness, not characteristic-two extension spectra. Retrieved mathematical-record items concern idempotent-free 2D examples or unrelated objects, and accessible earlier claims concern weighted-permutation statistics, not arbitrary binary structure matrices. General normal-basis and rational-canonical ingredients are classical and not claimed original. Residual risk: an undiscovered general theorem on semilinear fixed-point counts may already imply this application.

value.rationale: Idempotent elements are a natural invariant of nonassociative evolution algebras. The theorem gives an exact answer across all binary directed-graph structures and every finite binary field extension, including singular cases. It recovers the order of the nonnilpotent adjacency action from the extension-count sequence and resolves the detailed primary-block behavior, with explicit delayed appearance at degree seven. This is a motivated complete classification across a natural infinite class, not an isolated finite table; it does not claim a new normal-basis theorem.
